dedupe_keys.name: national primary flood defences base data and safety assessments nbpw waterveiligheidsportaal

description: The national base data on primary flood defences (Nationaal Basisbestand Primaire Waterkeringen, NBPW) gives a national overview of where every primary flood defence in the Netherlands lies, covering dikes, dams, dunes and hydraulic structures, with attributes such as the legal safety standard. Informatiehuis Water manages it for the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management and publishes it through the Waterveiligheidsportaal, together with the results of the national safety assessment and the reinforcement projects of the Flood Protection Programme (HWBP). The open Rijkswaterstaat WFS holds 4 NBPW layers, 80 layers from the first assessment round with verdicts and failure probabilities per failure mechanism, such as piping, macro-stability, grass cover erosion, dune erosion and closure reliability of structures, per dike section and trajectory, and 6 HWBP project layers; a REST API is also offered. Georegister metadata states no use limitations and no access conditions, so the services are free to use, with a revision in December 2024. Caveats: the second assessment round started in 2023 and its results are still being added, field lists per layer were not read, and portal functions beyond the open services need login. Simulation uses: fragility of flood defences by failure mechanism for breach and cascading flood models, exposure of the areas the defences protect, prioritising reinforcement and climate adaptation of the defence system. Related record: LIWO flood maps (data-netherlands-liwo-flood-information) give the inundation scenarios for breaches of these defences.
